task.name: bug: workspace setup is killed at an unconfigurable 120-second limit
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A sprint on the hdp project (forge v0.16.0rc8) failed in WORKSPACE before any
story was dispatched. The baseline workspace setup command was killed at exactly
120 seconds:

```
Workspace setup command failed: ...
```

The project's `workspace.setup_command` is `poetry install && npm ci && make
fixtures`. Re-running `make fixtures` by hand in the preserved baseline worktree
with warm caches took 11.4s, and the run had already gotten past `poetry install`
and `npm ci` and was inside fixtures when it was killed — so the chain normally
takes roughly 90–110 seconds cold, against a limit of 120.

`validation.gate_timeout: 1200` was set in `forge.yaml` and did not apply to
setup. There is no key in `forge.yaml` that raises the limit on workspace setup,
and the 120-second bound appears nowhere in the run's output before it is hit.

The same run recorded `observed_host_load=124.56` on a 10-core host at launch and
warned about contention, and expanded its gate timeout from 1200 to 2400 seconds
in response. Workspace setup received no equivalent expansion under the same
measured load.

No stories were dispatched, no branches were created, and the run cost nothing.
Re-running when the host is quiet succeeds or fails depending on how close the
setup chain lands to the 120-second mark.

The failure is not always terminal, and when it is not, it degrades scheduling
silently. On hdp run `5614af9f00a1` (2026-08-30, sprint `issues-427,428,429`) the
same 120-second timeout fired during batch preflight for two of the three stories,
and the sprint continued:

```
WARNING: batch preflight returned failure for issue-428: Workspace creation failed:
  Workspace setup command failed: TIMEOUT after 120s: ...; excluding from collision detection
WARNING: batch preflight returned failure for issue-427: Workspace creation failed:
  Workspace setup command failed: TIMEOUT after 120s: ...; excluding from collision detection
```

Those stories then carried no footprint, and the scheduler fell back to
serialising them:

```
Unknown footprint for issue-427 (empty/None likely_files): serializing
conservatively against known-footprint siblings
```

So a setup timeout can cost the sprint its collision detection and its
parallelism while the run still appears to proceed normally. The same timeout
appears in hdp runs on 2026-08-13, 08-19, 08-20, 08-28 and 08-30.

## Expected behavior

A workspace setup command runs whatever the patient project configured, so its
duration is a property of that project and not something Forge can know in
advance. Any bound Forge places on a project-supplied command therefore has to be
one the operator can discover and raise, in the same way the gate's bound is: a
limit that exists only as a constant, with no configuration key and no mention in
the output until the moment it fires, gives the operator no way to distinguish a
project that is genuinely stuck from one that is merely slower than an
undocumented default.

Where Forge already measures host contention at launch and scales a limit in
response, that measurement should govern every project-supplied command it
bounds, rather than one of them. A run that observes the host is oversubscribed
and widens one deadline while leaving another fixed will fail on the fixed one
under exactly the conditions it detected, and report that failure as though the
project command were at fault.

Failing this way should also be legible as a limit being reached rather than as
the command failing. The operator's first reading of the current message is that
their setup command broke.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `ad2fd15e3a7f44e9bb2dd0ad3ce0406b505cc9bb` captured at `2026-08-31T01:00:06.458559+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py` — `sha256:9c5ed787de305cccfaf0be7043a5e46d33aae7d1dc98f2edc57bc9609516d2ae`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/util.py` — `sha256:566d956ba187bfc48b44c14e68b62908b7d2c430ea3c706dc728f519a11d29ac`
- `src/theforge/sprint/gate_timeout_resolver.py` — `sha256:df39bd3dba7ed48abe372d04fceb7e11d9270565a819f15b32c3b43efb50034c`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:ca3a9879bb3ac9be277b14825e9471dbf0e940647941d8ce5badc261562297f6`
- `src/theforge/config/types.py` — `sha256:f9eb0dcaa761d498b716382ca83d9485fb96bfbe03209b5d4a075728fc7ac769`
- `docs/guides/inputs-reference.md` — `sha256:2dbec3ff7e0438ae096b6a5bd60fd6ef98e424219e17918c9838004d8d313bf2`
- `docs/guides/troubleshooting.md` — `sha256:0afbfd67981c5de726399eb5fd78c693c14be53a2c850acdd580b7d6c9dd6962`

### Observed symptom

Content class: confirmed symptom/evidence.
A sprint's WORKSPACE-phase setup command (workspace.setup_command, e.g.
"poetry install && npm ci && make fixtures") is killed at exactly 120 seconds
even though forge.yaml has no key that bounds or raises this limit, and the
120s figure is never surfaced to the operator before it fires. On the same
run, the gate timeout (validation.gate_timeout) was measured against host
load and expanded (1200s -> 2400s) in response to observed contention, but
the setup-command timeout received no equivalent adjustment and stayed fixed
at 120s under the same measured load.

### Reproduction / evidence

Content class: confirmed symptom/evidence.
Source inspection at HEAD (release/v0.16), traced end to end:

1. `src/theforge/coordinator/util.py:516-524` (`_run_shell_detailed`) and
   `util.py:645-653` (`_run_shell`) both declare `timeout: int = 120` as a
   plain parameter default, with no config-derived override anywhere in
   their signatures.
2. `src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:186-272` (`_run_setup_split`) is
   the sole executor of `workspace.setup_command`. Every one of its three
   `_cu._run_shell(...)` call sites (lines ~224, ~232, ~245, ~256, ~264) omits
   the `timeout=` keyword, so all of them fall through to the 120s default.
3. `_run_setup_split` is called from four sites in
   `coordinator/workspace.py` (`_create_workspace`, lines 1278, 1323, 1364,
   1398) and one site in `sprint/runner.py:1202` (the baseline workspace
   setup, run in WORKSPACE before any story is dispatched — matching the
   issue's report that no story was dispatched). None of these five call
   sites passes a `timeout=` argument either.
4. `src/theforge/config/types.py:476-490` (`WorkspaceConfig`) has fields
   for `create_command`, `base_branch`, `stale_worktree_days`, `auto_push`,
   `setup_command`, `python_interpreter` — no timeout field of any kind.
   There is no `workspace.setup_timeout` (or similarly named) key anywhere
   in the config schema, confirming the operator has no key to raise.
5. By contrast, `validation.gate_timeout` (`config/types.py:677`) plus
   `gate_timeout_scale`/`gate_cpu_cores` (lines 714-715) feed
   `resolve_effective_gate_timeout` in
   `src/theforge/sprint/gate_timeout_resolver.py:35-116`, which scales the
   gate's baseline timeout by a `factor` derived from `observed_host_load`
   (via `os.getloadavg()` at `sprint/runner.py:4959`). `sprint/runner.py:
   4977-5035` applies that resolution by rebinding
   `_ctx.config.validation.gate_timeout` before any story dispatch. This
   scaling mechanism exists and is wired only into the gate's timeout — it
   is never consulted by `_run_setup_split`/`_run_shell`, so the setup
   command's 120s bound does not participate in it.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** workspace.setup_command execution has a hardcoded 120s timeout with no forge.yaml key to configure it.
  - Evidence: _run_shell/_run_shell_detailed default timeout=120 (util.py:519,648); _run_setup_split's five internal call sites and all five of its external callers never pass timeout=; WorkspaceConfig (config/types.py:476-490) has no timeout field.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly inspected function signatures and call sites in the current checkout; not inferred from the issue text.
- **[ruled out]** The adaptive host-load scaling that widens validation.gate_timeout under contention is a general mechanism forge already applies to every project-supplied command, and setup_command's fixed 120s is just an oversight in an otherwise-general system.
  - Evidence: resolve_effective_gate_timeout and its call site in sprint/runner.py (~line 4977) operate only on _ctx.config.validation.gate_timeout; nothing in workspace.py or _run_setup_split reads _gate_timeout_resolution or observed_host_load. The scaling mechanism is gate-specific by construction, not a general host-load service that setup merely forgot to opt into — it was built once, for one caller, and setup_command was never given a path into it.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Grep across src/theforge for resolve_effective_gate_timeout and GateTimeoutResolution found only gate_timeout_resolver.py, sprint/runner.py, and their tests — no workspace-side consumer.
- **[inconclusive]** The failure message itself hides the fact that a timeout (not a command failure) occurred, matching the issue's framing that 'the operator's first reading is that their setup command broke.'
  - Evidence: _run_shell_detailed's TimeoutExpired branch (util.py:604-614) does prefix the returned output with 'TIMEOUT after {timeout}s: {cmd}', and workspace.py wraps it as 'Workspace setup command failed: TIMEOUT after 120s: ...' — so the eventual failure message does state a timeout occurred. What is genuinely absent is any advance mention of the 120s bound before it fires, and no forge.yaml key to discover or raise it, which is the issue's core, verifiable complaint.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly read the message-construction code; could not check the exact text of the hdp-project run's console output since hdp is a separate repository not present in this checkout.

### Confirmed cause

Content class: confirmed localization.
workspace.setup_command is executed through _run_setup_split
(src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py), whose underlying shell calls
(_cu._run_shell) rely on the hardcoded default timeout=120 declared in
_run_shell/_run_shell_detailed (src/theforge/coordinator/util.py). No
WorkspaceConfig field exists to override this value, and unlike
validation.gate_timeout — which sprint/runner.py scales via
resolve_effective_gate_timeout using observed host load before any story is
dispatched — the setup-command timeout is never fed into that (or any)
adaptive-scaling mechanism. A cold poetry install && npm ci && make fixtures
chain that normally lands at 90-110s is killed at exactly 120s whenever
variance or host contention pushes it over that fixed, unconfigurable, and
unscaled bound.

Support: Content class: confirmed localization support.
Directly observed in the current checkout: _run_shell_detailed's signature
(util.py:516-524) declares `timeout: int = 120`; _run_setup_split's five
_cu._run_shell call sites (workspace.py, inside the function body) never
pass timeout=; all five external callers of _run_setup_split
(coordinator/workspace.py _create_workspace x4, sprint/runner.py's baseline
setup call at line 1202) likewise never pass timeout=. WorkspaceConfig
(config/types.py:476-490) has no timeout-related field. The adaptive
scaling mechanism (gate_timeout_resolver.resolve_effective_gate_timeout,
invoked at sprint/runner.py:4977) reads and rewrites only
_ctx.config.validation.gate_timeout; grep confirms no other module consumes
it. This is a first-hand mechanism trace, not a restatement of the issue's
own narrative.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All supporting facts (default timeout value, omitted timeout= arguments, absent config field, gate-only scope of the scaling resolver) were observed directly in source at HEAD, not taken from the issue body's assertions.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/coordinator/util.py:519 (_run_shell_detailed timeout: int = 120),
src/theforge/coordinator/util.py:648 (_run_shell timeout: int = 120),
src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:186-272 (_run_setup_split — all
_cu._run_shell calls omit timeout=),
src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:1278,1323,1364,1398 (_create_workspace
call sites into _run_setup_split),
src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1202 (baseline workspace setup call site),
src/theforge/config/types.py:476-490 (WorkspaceConfig — no timeout field),
src/theforge/sprint/gate_timeout_resolver.py (adaptive scaling exists but is
gate-only; setup_command is not wired into it),
src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:4959-5035 (host-load measurement and
application, scoped to validation.gate_timeout only).

### Fix-success criterion

Content class: behavioral requirement for the eventual fix.
(1) An operator can raise the bound on workspace.setup_command's execution
time via a forge.yaml key, the same way validation.gate_timeout is
configurable today. (2) When the run measures host contention at launch (the
same observed_host_load signal that already scales validation.gate_timeout),
that measurement also governs the setup-command bound, so a run that widens
the gate timeout under detected contention does not leave the setup-command
timeout fixed under the same conditions. (3) The effective bound in force for
a given run is stated in the run's output before or at the moment setup
begins, not only discoverable after a failure. (4) A setup command that
legitimately runs longer than its old fixed 120s (e.g. the reported ~90-110s
cold chain under load) completes without being killed, given a bound sized
the way the gate's is.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- The TimeoutExpired failure path in _run_shell_detailed does embed 'TIMEOUT after {timeout}s' in its output, which somewhat undercuts (but does not fully refute) the issue's claim that the failure reads purely as a broken command; a fix that adds config + scaling should also consider whether this existing framing needs to be made more prominent (e.g. surfaced before the wrapping 'Workspace setup command failed:' prefix). (related: #2828)

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Content class: advisory, unverified repair proposal (not verified as part of
this investigation).
Consider adding a workspace.setup_timeout (or similarly named) key to
WorkspaceConfig mirroring validation.gate_timeout's shape, threading it
through _create_workspace/_run_setup_split/_cu._run_shell's timeout=
parameter instead of the current 120 default, and reusing
resolve_effective_gate_timeout (or a parameterized variant of it) against
the same observed_host_load measurement already computed in
sprint/runner.py before WORKSPACE runs, so both the gate and workspace setup
scale off one shared contention read. Not verified against config-loader
validation, schema-version bumps, or the baseline-gate call path's own
needs — a dev implementing this should re-check those before landing.

### Notes

Content class: investigation caveats/context.
The reported run itself (hdp project, forge v0.16.0rc8) lives in a separate
repository not present in this checkout, so I could not read its literal
audit/log output — the investigation is grounded entirely in tracing the
current theforge source (release/v0.16) that would have produced that
behavior. One nuance worth flagging for the fix author: _run_shell_detailed's
TimeoutExpired branch does prepend "TIMEOUT after {timeout}s: {cmd}" to the
returned output, so the eventual failure message is not entirely silent
about a timeout having occurred — the issue's stronger complaint (no
advance visibility, no config key) is what source inspection fully confirms;
the "operator reads it as their command breaking" framing is plausible but
not independently verified against the actual hdp console transcript.

handoff.summary: Added a configurable `workspace.setup_timeout` field, passed it explicitly through all workspace setup execution paths, logged the active bound when setup begins, and scaled it at sprint start from the same host-load measurement and adaptive/fixed policy used for `validation.gate_timeout`. The change also versioned the audit record to schema v40 with a migration that backfills the new recorded config entry for older records, regenerated the schema snapshot, and added seam-level tests covering config loading, sprint propagation, baseline setup, workspace timeout forwarding, and audit migration.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] No P1 regressions found; workspace setup timeout is configurable, logged, forwarded, and sprint-scaled before baseline, preflight, and dispatch. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Iteration 2 split the rebind so the workspace replace() is guarded by the dataclass check and the resolution line reports the bound actually in force; no regressions in the gate-timeout path, and all four fix-success criteria remain satisfied.

ac_verification.criterion: Symptom resolution: workspace setup commands are no longer killed by an unconfigurable, undisclosed, unscaled 120-second limit.
ac_verification.evidence: src/theforge/config/types.py:486 and src/theforge/config/_loaders.py:36 add and validate workspace.setup_timeout with the legacy 120-second default; src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:1282, src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:1332, src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:1378, and src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:1417 log the effective setup timeout and pass it into _run_setup_split for every story workspace creation path; src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:5013 resolves the workspace setup timeout with the same sprint scaling inputs as gate_timeout, src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:5083 rebinds the sprint config before src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:5345 baseline setup and src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:6058 batch preflight consume it, and src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1201 passes the configured timeout into baseline setup. Coverage includes tests/test_config_load.py:239 for config loading and validation, tests/test_coord_workspace_venv.py:44 for forwarding the timeout to shell calls, tests/test_sprint_baseline_gate.py:416 for baseline setup receiving and logging the configured timeout, and tests/test_sprint_gate_timeout_scaling.py:201 for scaled sprint config reaching dispatched work.

ac_verification.criterion: An operator can raise the bound on workspace.setup_command's execution time via a forge.yaml key, the same way validation.gate_timeout is configurable today.
ac_verification.evidence: config/types.py:486 adds setup_timeout to WorkspaceConfig; config/_loaders.py:36-47 and :119 validate and parse the forge.yaml key (rejects bool/non-int, rejects non-positive); defaults.py:182-184 and docs/guides/inputs-reference.md:719 document it. Tests in tests/test_config_load.py: test_workspace_setup_timeout_default_is_legacy_120, _valid_int_loads (480), _non_numeric_raises, _non_positive_raises.

ac_verification.criterion: When the run measures host contention at launch (the same observed_host_load signal that already scales validation.gate_timeout), that measurement also governs the setup-command bound.
ac_verification.evidence: sprint/runner.py:5013-5021 calls resolve_effective_gate_timeout with baseline=workspace.setup_timeout and the identical _host_cores, _gate_cpu_cores, _mode, len(_live_story_slugs) and _observed_host_load (os.getloadavg at runner.py:4964) used for the gate; runner.py:5082-5094 rebinds _ctx.config.workspace.setup_timeout, and _ctx.config is what run_task and run_batch_preflight (runner.py:6037-6039, the batch-preflight degradation described in the issue) receive. Tests: tests/test_sprint_gate_timeout_scaling.py::test_sprint_propagates_scaled_workspace_setup_timeout_to_run_task asserts cfg.workspace.setup_timeout == 252 (120 x factor 2.1 from gate_cpu_cores=7, parallel=3, host_cores=10), and ::test_sprint_skips_workspace_setup_timeout_rebind_for_non_dataclass_workspace pins the gate rebind (95) while the setup value stays 120.

ac_verification.criterion: The effective bound in force for a given run is stated in the run's output before or at the moment setup begins, not only discoverable after a failure.
ac_verification.evidence: runner.py:5036-5040 prints the "[sprint] workspace.setup_timeout: ..." resolution line at sprint start before any dispatch, and reports effective=<applied value> plus workspace_rebind=skipped when the value cannot be applied (runner.py:5025-5035); runner.py:1202-1206 logs "Running baseline workspace setup (timeout Ns): <cmd>"; workspace.py:1283-1286, 1333-1336, 1379-1382, 1418-1421 log the concrete timeout at each setup site. Tests: test_sprint_baseline_gate.py asserts the "(timeout 480s)" stderr line, and both scaling tests assert the sprint resolution line (including "candidate_effective=252s effective=120s").

ac_verification.criterion: A setup command that legitimately runs longer than its old fixed 120s (e.g. the reported ~90-110s cold chain under load) completes without being killed, given a bound sized the way the gate's is.
ac_verification.evidence: workspace.py:191 adds the timeout parameter to _run_setup_split and all five internal _cu._run_shell calls (lines 228, 237, 251, 263, 272) pass it instead of falling through to util.py's 120s default; all four _create_workspace sites (1292, 1342, 1388, 1427) and the baseline WORKSPACE site (runner.py:1211) pass timeout=config.workspace.setup_timeout. Tests: test_coord_workspace_venv.py::test_setup_timeout_is_forwarded_to_each_shell_call asserts timeouts == [321, 321] across both split shell calls, the reuse test asserts the timeout kwarg on _run_setup_split, and test_process_teardown_lifecycle.py asserts the reused-worktree path forwards config.workspace.setup_timeout.

finding_registry.description: Sprint start computes a _can_rebind_workspace guard and discards the setup-timeout resolution when the workspace config object is not a dataclass, but the context-rebind block still calls dataclasses.replace() on that same workspace object whenever the gate timeout changed, so the guard does not protect the path it was written for and the operator-visible [sprint] workspace.setup_timeout: line is still printed with an effective value that never takes effect.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
